description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and README.md:224 '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |' - the row immediately below README.md:223 '| CT01 | COTRN01 | COTRN01C | Transaction View |', so the project's own inventory assigns the two programs the opposite functions to the ones their mandated class names claim. The line is cited as 224 rather than the 222 this case's brief gives, because 222 is the CT00 transaction-list row; the citation was checked against the file rather than carried forward. That is the inverse of the prompt's mapping and the mirror image of parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. Rule R1 resolves it - the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source - and practice B4 governs the disclosure: the divergence is documented here and never silently corrected, the Agent Action Plan escalates it for explicit user confirmation, and no case in this folder is downgraded to read-only to match the name. WHAT THIS CASE PINS: the first-entry branch reached with a selection already made, the transaction-id-into-CARDNINI quirk it triggers, the second arm of VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS and that arm's IS NOT NUMERIC guard. EIBCALEN is 218 and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as '0', so NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER at :120 holds: :121 sets the re-enter flag, :122 moves LOW-VALUES to COTRN2AO, :123 moves -1 to ACTIDINL, and the test at :124-125 finds CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED neither SPACES nor LOW-VALUES, so :126-127 move it into CARDNINI and :128 performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. No AID is declared and none is needed - the first-entry branch is taken before the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :133-152 is reached at all - and :132's RECEIVE never runs, which is why mapFields is empty: nothing was typed on this screen. That is the ENTER-versus-REENTER nuance gate G38 asks for, and it is visible in one field: CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is '0' inbound and '1' outbound, set at :121 before the quirk ran, so the rejection this case pins is raised on the ENTER half of the pair while the screen it returns will arrive next time on the REENTER half. The CSSETATY highlight is not applied on either half - COTRN02C assigns exactly one attribute byte anywhere in its 783 lines, MOVE DFHGREEN TO ERRMSGC at :727 on the successful-write arm - so ERRMSGC is pinned at its default colour here. THE QUIRK, PRESERVED AND NOT REPAIRED (practice B5): a sixteen-byte selected TRANSACTION identifier is moved into the CARD NUMBER field. CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED is PIC X(16) at :80 and CARDNINI is PIC X(16) in app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, so the move is same-width and nothing is truncated - but the receiver is the card number, and map COTRN2A has no TRNIDIN item and no TRNID item at all: its twenty-one I-suffixed payload items are TRNNAMEI, TITLE01I, CURDATEI, PGMNAMEI, TITLE02I, CURTIMEI, ACTIDINI, CARDNINI, TTYPCDI, TCATCDI, TRNSRCI, TDESCI, TRNAMTI, TORIGDTI, TPROCDTI, MIDI, MNAMEI, MCITYI, MZIPI, CONFIRMI and ERRMSGI, and not one of them keys a transaction. So there is nothing to route the value to even if routing it were permitted, and it is not. Where the slot came from is visible in the source rather than guessed at: COTRN00C:62-70 declares the identical six-field extension as CDEMO-CT00-INFO, COTRN00C:151-178 move a listed row's TRNID0nI - a TRAN-ID - into CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SELECTED with no class test of any kind, and COTRN00C:185-195 evaluate the flag against 'S' and 's' and XCTL to COTRN01C. Nothing anywhere in app/cbl writes CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED, so COTRN02C reads a field that only a sibling program's layout ever fills, and the misdirected MOVE is what the source does with it. THE SELECTED VALUE, NAMED AND JUSTIFIED (practice B8): 'TRNX000000000001', exactly sixteen characters, four letters followed by twelve digits. It is non-numeric because COBOL's class test on a PIC X(16) item accepts the digits '0' to '9' and nothing else, so a single letter makes IS NUMERIC false. A selected identifier is entitled to look like this: TRAN-ID is PIC X(16) in app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy and TRNX-ID is PIC X(16) in app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY - the statement view of the same identifier, reached through the TRNXFILE DD at app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL:83 - so a transaction identifier is alphanumeric-capable by declaration, and the four leading characters are that repository's own token for one. The selection path applies no class test to it (COTRN00C:151-178) even though the list screen does test its own typed key field at COTRN00C:209-218, which is exactly how a non-numeric identifier reaches this guard. The literal is also deliberately a different malformed shape from case12's dotted '1.2.3           ', so the two rejections cannot both be satisfied by one reading of the class test. THE THREE KEY-FIELD ARMS AND WHO OWNS THEM, RECONCILED AGAINST THE FOLDER AS BUILT (practice B4): VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS is an ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :195-230 whose first match wins (gate G30). Arm one at :196 takes the account identifier when ACTIDINI is neither spaces nor low-values, and it is owned by case08 ('Account ID must be Numeric...'), case09 ('Account ID NOT found...') and case10 ('Unable to lookup Acct in XREF AIX file...'), with case13 through case20 traversing it successfully on their way to the data-field checks and the write. Arm two at :210 takes the card number, and it is owned by THIS case on the first-entry route and by case12 on the REENTER route; case03 traverses it successfully with a numeric selection. Arm three, the WHEN OTHER at :224, is owned by case07 ('Account or Card Number must be entered...'). This case's authoring brief numbered those owners one lower - arm three at case06, arm one at case07 to case10, arm two at case11 to case14 - which is off by one against the twenty cases that exist: case06 drives the EVALUATE EIBAID WHEN OTHER with DFHPF12, and case13 and case14 drive the amount and origination-date format checks inside VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS rather than the key arms. The allocation is corrected here in the open rather than restated wrongly, because a case that misnames its neighbours sends the next reader to the wrong file. Arm one being evaluated before arm two is also why this case leaves ACTIDINI untouched: :122's LOW-VALUES is what makes arm one fail its test, and without that the card path would never be reached. THE FUNCTION NUMVAL SEMANTICS, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE CASE (gate G29): the rejection is owned by the IS NOT NUMERIC guard at :211 and NOT by the intrinsic. :212-216 move 'Y' to WS-ERR-FLG, move the literal to WS-MESSAGE, move -1 to CARDNINL and PERFORM SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN - and SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN ends at :530-534 with EXEC CICS RETURN, which in CICS terminates the task. Control therefore never reaches :218, so COMPUTE WS-CARD-NUM-N = FUNCTION NUMVAL(CARDNINI) is never invoked on malformed text; :220-221 never renormalise the field; READ-CCXREF-FILE at :222 never runs, so neither of the cross-reference call sites is reached and no RESP arm of :621-637 is entered (gate G47 in its negative form); and :223's MOVE XREF-ACCT-ID TO ACTIDINI never happens. NUMVAL only ever sees a string the class test has already proved to be all digits. A translation that rendered the PERFORM as a call and then fell through to the next statement - which is what a naive reading of the paragraph produces, because COBOL's PERFORM does return to its caller when the performed paragraph does not end the task - would hand garbage to the intrinsic and then either throw or silently coerce, and would additionally read the cross-reference on a rejected screen. THE MALFORMED-INPUT VARIANT SURFACE this guard rejects, enumerated rather than left implied (practice B1): alphabetic characters, as here; an embedded space, such as case08's '0000000 050' on the account arm; a stray '+' or '-', because the class test on an alphanumeric item accepts no operational sign, so a signed string is not numeric; a decimal point, as in case12's '1.2.3'; and a value shorter than the field, space-padded on the right by the MOVE, where the trailing spaces are themselves what makes it non-numeric. An all-spaces value cannot reach this guard at all, from either direction: :124-125 excludes SPACES and LOW-VALUES before the quirk can move anything, and arm two's own test at :210 excludes them again, so a blank selection reaches :130's send with an empty screen instead - which is case02. WHAT IS ASSERTED, AND WHY EACH VALUE IS WHAT IT IS: CARDNINO carries 'TRNX000000000001' exactly as the quirk moved it in, unrenormalised, because the renormalising MOVE at :220-221 is unreachable. ACTIDINO carries eleven low-values: :122 moved LOW-VALUES across the whole output group and :223 - the only statement that would fill it on this path - never runs, so the field is not blank in the sense of spaces but binary zero, and the same is true of the twelve detail items TTYPCDO, TCATCDO, TRNSRCO, TDESCO, TRNAMTO, TORIGDTO, TPROCDTO, MIDO, MNAMEO, MCITYO, MZIPO and CONFIRMO, each at the width its PICTURE clause declares. There is exactly ONE message, 'Card Number must be Numeric...', and it is pinned on both of the channels the send publishes it on (rule R5): WS-MESSAGE is PIC X(80) at :38 and ERRMSGO is PIC X(78) in the symbolic map, so MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO at :520 loses the two rightmost bytes, and reporting only one channel would make that loss unobservable. Both are the same thirty-character literal, left justified and space padded. THE CURSOR is reported on ACTIDINL, not on CARDNINL, and the reason matters: both length items hold -1 by the time the screen is sent - ACTIDINL from :123 and CARDNINL from :215 - and where more than one length item holds -1 the terminal places the cursor in the FIRST such field in map declaration order, which is ACTIDIN. app/bms/COTRN02.bms:85 says the same thing a second way: ACTIDIN is declared ATTRB=(FSET,IC,NORM,UNPROT), and IC marks it the initial-cursor field, while CARDNIN at :104 carries no IC. This case's brief supposed instead that the later write would win; it does not, and the correction is recorded here rather than applied silently, because a cursor on the wrong field is a visible defect on a real 3270. Both writes are nonetheless accounted for: the length items are validation and highlight metadata and are never JSON payload members, so CARDNINL's -1 is stated in this prose and ACTIDINL's -1 is what cursorField carries. Nothing is written anywhere: expectedWrites is empty, which is the positive assertion that the backward browse at :644-704 and the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 were not reached, TRANSACT stands byte for byte as seeded across all three of its 350-byte rows, the return code is 0 because COTRN02C sets none and contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD', and no nextProgram other than this program's own name appears because the task ended at RETURN TRANSID('CT02') rather than at an XCTL. THE HEADER SIX AND THE PINNED CLOCK (practice B7): SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN performs POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :518, which at :554-571 moves CCDA-TITLE01 and CCDA-TITLE02 from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy into TITLE01O and TITLE02O at their declared PIC X(40), WS-TRANID 'CT02' into TRNNAMEO, WS-PGMNAME 'COTRN02C' into PGMNAMEO, and the current date and time into CURDATEO as MM/DD/YY and CURTIMEO as HH:MM:SS. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 - the single instant all twenty cases in this folder use - so CURDATEO is 07/19/22 and CURTIMEO is 23:12:34 in any timezone and on any day the suite runs. THE 218-BYTE AREA AND THE 58-BYTE EXTENSION (rule R6, gate G37, practice B11): app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy sums to 4+8+4+8+8+1+1+9+25+25+25+11+1+16+7+7 = 160 bytes and the CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension at COTRN02C:72-80 sums to 16+16+8+1+1+16 = 58, so the area this transaction passes is 218 bytes and eibcalen says so. The extension is a SEPARATE payload field in the translation and is never folded into the 160-byte NavigationContext that all seventeen online programs share - widening that shared type to suit one program would put a CT02-only slot into sixteen screens that have no use for it - and this case is the folder's primary exerciser of the separation, because the selection carried in the extension is what drives the whole path. All six sub-fields are therefore populated explicitly rather than left to default: CDEMO-CT02-TRNID-FIRST '0000000000000001' and CDEMO-CT02-TRNID-LAST '0000000000000003' are the first and last identifiers of the three seeded TRANSACT rows, CDEMO-CT02-PAGE-NUM is 00000001 at its PIC 9(08) width, CDEMO-CT02-NEXT-PAGE-FLG is 'N' - the value :76 gives it a VALUE clause for, and the 88-level NEXT-PAGE-NO - CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SEL-FLG is 'S', the selection flag COTRN00C:186-187 accepts, and CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED is the sixteen-byte literal above. All twenty-two fields of the area are pinned on the way out and none is omitted, because the conversation state travels in the payload rather than in a server-side session and an unpinned field is a field nobody has checked; every one of the six comes back unchanged, which is what proves the extension made the round trip. THE DATASETS THIS CASE SEEDS, AND WHY: CCXREF is seeded from the first five rows of cardxref.txt exactly as they ship, 36 bytes wide, and is deliberately NOT pre-padded - app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares CARD-XREF-RECORD as 16+9+11+14 = 50 and the fixture omits the trailing FILLER PIC X(14), so the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below supplies those fourteen spaces once, at seed time, and is the sole owner of that repair (gate G16, risk R-F). Nothing pads again at comparison time. The rows are real data and none of them could match a non-numeric key in any case, which is beside the point here: the read never happens. CXACAIX is not seeded as a dataset of its own, because app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines it as a PATH over the CCXREF base - an alternate-index finder, never a second table (gate G45). TRANSACT is seeded with three inline 350-byte rows because no ASCII fixture ships for that master - it is populated online, not loaded - and each row is summed from app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy as 16+2+4+10+100+11+9+50+50+10+16+26+26+20 with the trailing FILLER PIC X(20) present and space-filled (gates G19 and G21). Every dataset is addressed by its application.yml binding key, so not one fully-qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file (gate G46); no tenth fixture is named, the fixture set being closed at the nine derived from app/data/ASCII; and the code page is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION AND IS NOT SEEDED (practice B5): WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' is declared at :40 and COPY CVACT01Y at :89, and neither is referenced anywhere in the program - no DATASET operand names WS-ACCTDAT-FILE and no field of ACCOUNT-RECORD is ever moved - so the account master is a dead declaration and its copybook a dead include, and no case in this folder may expect an ACCTDAT read or place an ACCTDAT row in an expectation. This case's brief listed acctdata.txt among the inputs to seed; it is not seeded, and the reason is recorded rather than acted on silently (practice B4). ParityHarness.seed states that the inputs member names every dataset the unit under test will read, so seeding a master this program never opens would assert a read that does not exist - and because the harness refuses only unconsumed forced outcomes, not unconsumed inputs, that false assertion would have passed unnoticed, which is precisely the failure mode worth avoiding. The deadness is asserted as the non-event it is, and COTRN02CParityTest.DeadDeclarations separately proves the translation keeps both names as constants and wires no account collaborator at all. CASE ALLOCATION, RECONCILED IN THE OPEN (practice B4): this slot previously encoded the cross-reference miss on the CCXREF base path - a numeric card number typed on the REENTER route, read at :222 and rejected by :624-629 with 'Card Number NOT found...'. This case supersedes it with the behaviour its brief assigns, which no other case in the folder covers: case03 drives the quirk route with a numeric selection and reaches the data-field checks, and case12 drives arm two's guard from the REENTER route, but the combination - the quirk route with a NON-numeric selection, so the key guard fires before any dataset is touched and the cursor lands on ACTIDINL rather than on the rejected field - was pinned nowhere. The displaced behaviour is not left unchecked: TransactionViewControllerTest asserts 'Card Number NOT found...' at its own call site, so the :624-629 arm remains driven and the branch-coverage gate is unaffected; what changes is which of the twenty declarative cases owns it. Recording the move is the whole point - a reallocation nobody wrote down is indistinguishable from a coverage hole. BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of MAIN-PARA, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts (app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy 160 bytes and the :72-80 extension 58, so 218; app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy 350; app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy 50), against the symbolic-map widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY (twenty-one I-suffixed payload items, ACTIDINI PIC X(11), CARDNINI PIC X(16), ERRMSGO PIC X(78); the L-suffixed length items and the flag and attribute items carry metadata and are never payload), against the DFHMDF definitions of app/bms/COTRN02.bms, and against the real bytes of app/data/ASCII. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, which Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers - among them a compiler whose indexed-file handler is disabled, the absence of any Language Environment CEE service behind the CSUTLDTC this program calls at :393 and :413, the absence of a CICS emulator, and the absence of the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA copybooks it copies at :92-93 - and the change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. NO USER RULES EXIST: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided', and that line is the whole document, so no rule forces this file into scope and no rule constrains how it is written. The absence is stated explicitly and is not treated as permission to lower the bar: the standard held here is the Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 enterprise practices, cited by name where they bite - B1 (every literal derived and verified, the malformed-input variants enumerated rather than left implied, and no placeholder anywhere), B3 (the reference trees app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd and app/data are read-only and were not touched), B4 (the R-B inversion, the arm-owner renumbering, the ACCTDAT non-seed, the cursor correction and the case reallocation all disclosed), B5 (the quirk, the dead declarations and the digits-only class test all preserved rather than tidied), B7 (a pinned clock), B8 (binding keys, a named code page, all six extension sub-fields populated and the selected literal named), B11 (every width summed from a PICTURE clause) and B12 (the provenance statement above). Rules R1, R5, R6 and R7 bind as cited: R7 in particular is discharged by the EVALUATE order this case depends on, and COTRN02C contains no GO TO to restructure. GATES DISCHARGED: G15 (one of exactly twenty cases in parity/COTRN02C), G16 (the cardxref seed stays 36 bytes and is normalised once at seed time, never pre-padded), G18 (the diff count must be zero, per module rather than per build), G19 and G21 (350-byte TRANSACT rows whose FILLER is present and space-filled), G29 (the mandatory FUNCTION NUMVAL rejection on the card path, discharged by proving the intrinsic is never invoked), G30 (the ordered EVALUATE TRUE at :195-230 with arm one before arm two), G37 (no server-side session state - the whole 218-byte area travels in the payload), G38 (the ENTER half of the pair, with CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT '0' inbound and '1' outbound), G45 (CXACAIX is an alternate-index finder over the CCXREF base, not a second table), G46 (binding keys, never a dataset-name literal), G47 (both cross-reference call sites proven NOT reached) and G51 (the controller is driven as a plain object - no MockMvc, no servlet container and no HTTP in the path). DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED, because COTRN02C has none of them: G32 (zero GO TO, so no backward jump to restructure), G35 (zero CALL 'CEE3ABD', which is why the return code is 0 and no abend path exists), G39 (no pagination loop on this screen) and G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC). G40 does not apply either: no XCTL is reached on this path, so no nextProgram other than this program's own is resolved.
